submissions.title: Memphis City Council declines to pass data center moratorium
submissions.excerpt: Council voted down a year-long moratorium but passed an ordinance putting a 135-day pause on data centers.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: concerns tracked project xAI Colossus 2 (Memphis, TN). On 2026-10-20 the Memphis City Council rejected a 12-month data center moratorium (Ordinance 19, tied 6-6) but passed a separate ordinance (Ordinance 18, 7-5) imposing a 135-day pause on NEW data center approvals, paired with Mayor Paul Young's 90-day executive-order review of digital infrastructure impacts. Multiple outlets (WREG, WSMV, Baxtel, Daily Memphian) report the pause does not apply to xAI's existing/already-approved facilities, so Colossus 2 construction itself is not halted, but any new expansion filings in the city would be. submissions.title: Investing in Wyoming's infrastructure, energy and workforce
submissions.excerpt: Google will invest $17 billion in its first data center in Wyoming, a campus in Laramie County near Cheyenne.
submissions.note: New project, not currently tracked. Google announced (via its own blog, Nov 5 2026, authored by VP Steve Walter) its first Wyoming data center: a $17B investment on 716 acres in the Switchgrass Industrial Park, Laramie County, near Cheyenne (previously known pre-disclosure as 'Project Tembo'/'Project Jade'). The $17B figure is Google's own total-investment statement. SEPARATELY, Google says it will fund a 702 MW fuel-cell-with-carbon-capture generation project (with Bloom Energy, Tallgrass Energy, Black Hills Energy and AEP as partners) to supply the campus — that 702 MW is a GENERATION figure, not confirmed site IT load. Third-party trackers (Cowboy State Daily, via local reporting predating Google's own confirmation) have cited a much larger ~2.7 GW total site-power figure for the campus, which Google itself has not confirmed; treat that figure as unconfirmed/analyst estimate, not primary. submissions.title: Amazon's proposed data center application deemed complete by Walla Walla County
submissions.excerpt: three buildings of 220,000 sq ft each on 134 acres, with an expected 300 MW capacity
submissions.note: New project, not currently tracked (AWS's first announced Washington State site). Amazon Data Services ('Amazon Attalia' campus) plans three buildings (220,000 sq ft each) on 134 of the 554 acres it bought from the Port of Walla Walla in Feb 2026 ($36M), at Wallula Gap Business Park, Walla Walla County, WA, with an expected 300 MW capacity. This is a scale-down from an earlier-reported $4.8B/16-building plan for the same land, so treat the larger figure as superseded, not additive. SITING RESTRICTION angle: the county deemed the land-use application complete (Sept 2026) but has NOT approved it — a SEPA environmental review is still pending with no decision timeline, and a local group (Walla Walla Anti-Data Center League) has collected ~1,900 signatures on petitions for a county data-center moratorium that could affect this project before it's approved. submissions.title: Boise City Council approves 6-month moratorium on large data center construction
submissions.excerpt: a six-month moratorium applies to facilities larger than 100,000 square feet or with at least 20 megawatts demand
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION, new — not tied to a currently tracked project (no tracked project is sited in Boise, ID). On 2026-11-10 the Boise City Council voted unanimously to approve an emergency 6-month moratorium on new large data center applications, proposed by Mayor Lauren McLean. It covers facilities over 100,000 sq ft or with a projected power demand of at least 20 MW at full buildout; the city says it currently has no mega-data-center applications pending, and is using the window to write zoning/code standards and study water, energy, wastewater, noise and public-safety impacts. Reported as not affecting projects with pre-existing planning permission.
